citation: Glessner House Museum, 'Mattie Williamson, the Glessners' beloved cook', The Story of a House (blog), 31 March 2020.
author: Glessner House Museum
locator: The whole post: her hiring as a maid, her promotion to cook in early February 1892, her break of May 1897 to about May 1898, and her marriage to William Prescott in Los Angeles on 26 December 1912.
access_notes: Read 2026-10-30 (T-3253) through a fetch that returned the text in short quoted segments. No archived snapshot verified.
note: The museum's account of the Glessners' cook, written from Frances Glessner's journal. It names her as Martha L. Williamson, 'Mattie', cook from February 1892 until she left to marry in 1912, apart from a year away in 1897-98, and says she cooked for 'the live-in staff of eight' as well as the family. It also names Fanny Tynan, who worked for the family 'on and off' for over twenty years, without dating her service to 1904.
what_it_supplies: the Glessners' cook in 1904, by a service range that covers it
the size of the Glessners' live-in staff, eight, in her years as cook
what_it_does_not_supply: the names of the other seven live-in staff in 1904
